newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Angola's debt picks up as unity govt cheers market.
newsitem.headline: Angola's debt picks up as unity govt cheers market.

text.p: The price of Angolan debt has increased in the last week following the installation of the country's first government of national unity earlier this month, analysts said on Monday.

"Angola seems to be turning around, the civil war is finished and its seems it is cleaning up its act and this is bringing international attention to Angola," Investec Securities' sub-Saharan analyst Matthew Pearson told Reuters.
Defaulted debt from the country's national bank, Angola BNA West was being quoted at 30/31 cents in the dollar from 29/30 cents a week ago.
Debt issued by the state's oil company Angola Sonangol was quoted at 92/95 cents to the dollar compared to the previous week's 90/92 cents.

Angola's ruling MPLA, led by President Jose Eduardo dos Santos, and former rebel movement UNITA, headed by Jonas Savimbi, inaugurated the unity government on April 11, after they agreed in a U.N.-brokered 1994 peace accord.
